Figured I'd get some content going here, starting with a set that I haven't really seen much discussion about before.

Psycho-Pass

Psycho-Pass (PP) is a 36 card EB, with 3 PRs, from 2013. It's a set that is generally considered to be one of the weaker sets, but at the same time it's a set I quite enjoy. The set generally lacks good level 1, specifically in utility to build your late game hand while keeping a field, as well as good level 3 options. In my opinion though, the level 0 is pretty decent and there are a couple of decent climax combos that can get you through to the late game. I also really like the flavour that some of the cards have, something that you will discover if you have seen the anime.

The other annoying thing about the set is that there are 2 traits that are shared across the 36 cards. This can make deck construction more limited due to some cards requiring that you have specific traits on the field. The main trait is Public Safety, shared by every red card. This is the main trait that most decks focus on. Psycho-Pass is the other major trait, attributed to all blue cards, as well as most of the red cards. A deck will more than likely need a balance of both of these.

So, into the cards.

Level 0

"Lemonade Candy" Akane

Yeah, it's a vanilla level 0 bomb. Great way to start this off, right? One of your main level 0 non-utility cards, as the nature of it being a vanilla gives it an extra 500 power. With an assist and Yayoi you can get up around 3500, which can allow you to get over your apponent's level 0 on your turn, then force them to run in on theirs. Can also be buffed by the bond we will see soon.

Kougami, Enforcer

Standard loner, gaining 1500 when it's alone in the front row. Generally not one of my favourites as I like to build a decent amount of stock before level 1 with this deck, but it's also a good pick for those few slots at level 0.

Yayoi Kunizuka

Interesting card, giving +1000 and a level to another character on play. This can allow you to get around level 0 bombs, level 1 bombs or just give power later in the game. Keep in mind it cannot buff itself though.

"A Beast to Hunt a Beast" Kougami

One of my favourite level 0s in this set. Allows you to grab one of the better 1/1s for the cost of a card in your hand, while also giving all Akane (of which there aren't many) 500 extra power.

Makishima, Cold Glare

Damage yourself to get a level 2 or above. Important card, as it is one of the few reliable ways for you to grab your late game. If this grabbed level 1 or lower though, I believe the set would be quite a bit stronger. And Makishima generally has Book trait, just fyi.

Makishima, Refined Intelligence

Plussing brainstorm for draw. Probably the best brainstorm in the set, shame it doesnt at least allow you to grab a Psycho-Pass character, but it is what it is.

Shion Karanomori

The other brainstorm in the set, standard spammable hand-filtering brainstormerino for Public Safety. Keep in mind it does not have Psycho-Pass, which can be important at level 1 when it comes down to counters. Non-foil art is better, which makes me sad.

Nobuchika Ginoza

First assist to note, at 500 in front. At first, it seems like the top effect is pointless, but this having Psycho-Pass and Public Safety can be quite important, as you will see. Glasses

"Smile of Saint" Makishima

500 global that can't be targetted. Seems strictly better than the above, but the Public Safety of Ginoza can be surprisingly important. Not being targettable is interesting, but rarely useful.

"Hound three" Kougami,

Makishima, Mysterious Man,

Akane, Rookie Inspector

Vanillas, the last of which is a CD PR.

Level 1

You have a number of different routes to take at level 1, none of which are really that amazing, but depend on what style of play you want.

Akane, Talent for Inspector

The bond from before searches this card. Generally it's an 8k+ beater, so can get over basically every 1/0 in existence and a number of level 1s. No Psycho-Pass trait though, so be weary of that.

Kougami, Back When He Was Inspector

Average. Your level 1 often relies on backups, so there's not much of a reason to run this. Maybe as a 1 of in some decks.

Kougami, Target to Seek

The only hand encore in the set. Draw phase changes into this, which is interesting. The way I look at it is you basically pay 2 to pull out a 2/2. You often also drop a card cause the change puts a huge target on it's back and... it's a 6k 1/1. You usually get the 2/2 at the end of level 1 or the start of level 2, at which time you could have played it for 2 and not dropped a card. It also can't front if you don't have an Akane, so, if you get it out at level 1, you will need to side for 1 most of the time due to not running the above Akane.

Makishima, A Rose

1/1 vanilla clock encore. Decent, but I think it works best with another 1/1 as I'm not a fan of fielding 2-3 clock encores at 1 stock each.

Kougami, Determination Towards Investigation

The only real way to generate advantage at level 1. Combos with the +2 soul, but does cost stock, so don't overuse it.

"Criminally Asymptomatic" Makishima

Climax combo with the brutal 2k1 to filter a card in your hand for a Psycho-Pass. I don't really find this to be useful because you often don't have excess cards in your hand at this point of the game. It's also a 1/1.

Kougami During Training

A decent 1/0 option, for this set at least. Very weak on the defence.

Makishima, Emotional Tuning

A PR that is quite good on the defence. You can run the 2 soul, side with this, then try to save it with a backup. Sadly, no foil though.

Shuusei Kagari

I like the foil version. A lot. Kagari was quite a cool character. But, this card isn't great. Basically a 7500 1/1 that kills itself at the end of your turn, compressing your deck. Keep in mind it is spammable, but even so, I'm still not a fan.

Makishima, Resistance Towards the Controlling Society

Draw phase change for 4 and a card. Good if it works, but with the prevelance of anti-change, don't think it's worth it.

Che Guzon

2k splittable backup. The criteria is easily fulfilled with even just a Ginoza and a Kougami of some sort. Useful even into the late game, protecting your level 3 Kougamis that get strong on their own.

Level 2

Kougami, Seeing the Depth

The best level 2 filler we have, if you aren't planning on running encores up to level 3 or running the change to the 2/2. Philosophical flavor text. Yeah.

Kougami, Bouquet of Roses

The 2/2 that the hand encore level 1 changes into. The level assist Akane fulfils the criteria, or a 1/1.

Makishima, Undercover as Art Teacher

If you have a way to reliably have 5 or more cards in your hand at level 2 with this deck and not lose, let me know. I'm probably playing the game wrong.

Makishima, Deep Foresight

A clock encore 2/3. Seems useless, but can be used in combination with this event that will be discussed later.

Akane Tsunemori

My choice of level 2 assist. And not just because it has an SP. Not being targetable is interesting, and actually a little bit relevant when it comes to allowing your level 3s to stand. Climax combo with the gate, which is good cause you can run 3 or 4 gates and then use the combo if you ever need it. It isn't a game changer, but can be surprisingly useful at times.

"Latent Criminal" Kougami

The other assist at level 2. 1k in front is as good as the above Akane for the level 3 Makishima as this has Psycho-Pass, while the Akane does not. Has a climax phase change with the red 2k1 into the level 3 Kougami, and can send your opponent's level 3s to memory before you change it. Decent card, but not my choice.

Tomomi Masaoka

Pops backup. Cool foil art.

Sibyl System

Interesting 2/0 event. You can switch a level 2 on your stage for a 2/3 clock encore, but in the end, not too useful as you need to get this card and the other level 2 onto the stage just to bring out what is basically a vanilla. If you use it on either of the level 3s, they won't get their on play effects either.

Kougami, Pattern of the Executor

Another CD PR vanilla.

Level 3

Shinya Kougami

The best level 3 in the set. Heals and gets to 13k+ with a level 2 Akane. The reason I run Ginoza Is that having him plus a single level 2 Akane allows Kougami to stand, no matter what, after your opponent's turn. Having a global Makishima and an Akane will often mean that he will not stand, as Kougami may be the only thing to survive. And there's a pseudo-change, as well as an SP.

Shuugo Makishima

The other level 3 in the set. Cantripping allows you to keep up cards in hand, something often useful with this set. Also gets relativelty strong, as all cards except Akanes should buff it. The combo with the book is interesting, and the only thing we have relatively close to a "finisher", but it does not allow you to end games by any stretch of the imagination.

Final thoughts

The set is by no means strong, but once again, I do enjoy it. We can hope for a movie set, or even a season 2 set, but that will probably never happen. My choices for the deck are 1/1 akane, 1/0 +2 soul Kougami and 1/0 PR Makishima, along with 4 Che Guzons. I run 4 2 soul, 3 gate and 1 book, but this is always changing.

Finally, run foils.
